title: Neighboring Bitwise XOR
description: A 0-indexed binary array `derived` of length `n` is formed from a hidden binary array `original` of length `n` by taking the cyclic pairwise XOR of adjacent elements: for `0 <= i < n - 1`, `derived[i] = original[i] XOR original[i + 1]`, and for `i = n - 1`, `derived[n - 1] = original[n - 1] XOR original[0]`. Given `derived`, return `true` if there exists at least one valid binary array `original` that produces `derived`, or `false` otherwise.
hints: Take the XOR of all elements in `derived`: every `original[i]` appears exactly twice in the product.
Because each `original[i]` cancels itself out, a valid `original` exists if and only if the XOR of all entries in `derived` equals 0.

examples.explanation: Total XOR of [1, 0] is 1 != 0, so no cyclic binary array can produce it.
